JUDGMENT
This claim petition is filed under Sec.166 of M.V Act, 1988 seeking compensation for the death caused in a Road Traffic accident.

2. The case of the petitioners in the nutshell is that on 30.12.2023 at about 11.00 a.m, the deceased who was riding a motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-34-W-7520 along with Pillion ride by name Smt.
Rudramma in slowly and cautiously by observing all the traffic rules and regulations on the left side of New Bypass road, Rupanagudi road, while so proceeding and reached Opposite to Vasu field,
Tirumalanagar Camp, New Bypass road, Rupanagudi road, Bellari, a Trailer lorry bearing Reg.No.KA-01-A-8304 was parked in the middle of the road without showing any signal / indication i.e., without putting any cautionary board.
When the deceased reached close to the lorry, he learnt that it was stationary and tried to avoid the collision.
But till then it was too late and he could not control his vehicle and thereby dashed against the rear portion of the Trailer lorry.
Due to the tremendous impact the deceased fell down along with his motorcycle and sustained multiple injuries all over the body.
Immediately after the accident he was shifted to hospital, but he was succumbed to the fatal injuries and died on the same day at about 12.10 p.m, while undergoing treatment.
It is submitted that postmortem was conducted and corpse was handed over to the family members.

It is submitted that because of untimely death of deceased, the petitioners have suffered economically as well as emotionally and due to unexpected death of deceased, they have undergone mental agony and shock and lost bread earning member of the family.
The respondent No.1 & 2 being the owner and insurer of the offending Trailer lorry.

The accident was occurred due to rash and negligent act of the driver of the offending Trailer lorry and as such, the respondent No.1 & 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioners.
Contending the above facts, they pray to grant for compensation with interest and cost.
3. The respondent No.1 though entered appearance through his counsel, he failed to contest the matter by filing the written statement.
4. The respondent No.2 appeared through his counsel and filed written statement admitting the issuance of insurance policy in respect of Trailer lorry bearing Reg.No.KA-01-A-8304.
However the liability if any is pleaded to be subject to the terms & conditions of the policy.
This respondent specifically and empathically denied the occurrence, mode and manner of accident and also involvement of the vehicle in the accident.
Without prejudice, it is further contended that there was no negligence on the part of the driver of insured vehicle.

Infact the accident occurred due to the sole negligence & reckless driving of the deceased himself he was without maintaining the safe Surekha vs Muthar Pasha .M.F on 8 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/40758423/
2 distance between the vehicles and without having proper lookout the vehicular movements of the road in carelessly and in the process he lost control and hit the stationed vehicle from behind and caused the accident.
Further the deceased was riding his motorcycle that too without wearing a helmet and without possessing DL.
As such the the deceased himself was responsible for the accident and who is the tortfeasor for his own negligence.

Non -compliance of section's 134(c),
158(6), 147 and 149 of MV Act is pleaded.
Without prejudice to the said contention it is averred that the driver of the lorry did not possess valid & effective DL and the insured is not possess valid FC and Permit as on the date of accident.
Despite knowing the said fact the owner thereof had handed over its possession to such a driver.
On account of willful breach of the terms & conditions of the policy by the insured, the insurance company is not liable to indemnify him.
Rest of the petition averments are contended as false and baseless and it is prayed to dismiss the petition.

5. On the basis of the above pleadings the following issues were framed :
ISSUES 1) Whether the petitioners proves that they are the legal heirs and dependents of the deceased ?
2) Whether the petitioners prove

that the deceased succumbed to the injuries sustained in a road traffic accident that occurred on 30.12.2023 at about 11.00 a.m.,
Opposite Vasu Field, Tirumala Nagar Camp, New Bypass road, Rupanagudi Road,
Bellary District, due to actionable negligence of the driver of Trailer Lorry bearing Reg.No.KA-01- A-8304

? 
3) Whether the petitioners are entitled for compensation as prayed ?
If so, at what rate and from whom ?
4) What order or award ?
6. Petitioner No.1 examined herself as PW.1.
Ex's. P1
to 12 and
Ex.P.15 to 20 were marked on behalf of the petitioners.
The petitioners have also examined the witness to prove the avocation of deceased as PW.2, through him got marked Ex.P.13 and 14 and Ex.P.21 documents.
In order to prove the defence, the respondent No.2 got examined its officer as RW.1 and got marked Ex.R.1 & 2 documents.
7. Heard arguments of both sides.
Perused the entire materials placed on record and arguments.

My answers to the above issues are as follows :-
 Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative  Issue No.2 : Partly in the Affirmative  Issue No.3 : Partly in the Affirmative  Issue No.4 : As per final order for the Surekha vs Muthar Pasha .M.F on 8 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/40758423/
3  following :
 REASONS 8. ISSUE NO.2 : The occurrence of the accident on the relevant date, time and place is not in dispute.
The only issue with which the parties are at loggerheads is with regard to the factum of negligence.

Perusal of the evidence on record makes it evident that deceased was riding the motorcycle opposite to Vasu field, Tirumala Nagar Camp, New Bypass road, Rupanagudi road,
Bellary and dashed against the rear side of the lorry bearing Reg.No.KA-01-A-8304 that was negligently parked on the said road.
This collision resulted in the occurrence of the accident.

The jurisdictional police conducted thorough investigation and laid charge sheet against both the rider /
deceased and driver of Lorry for the offences punishable u/s's 279, 283, 337 & 304(A) of IPC and u/s 187, 146, 196. 52 and 192 of IMV Act.
There is nothing on record to believe that the charge sheet filed by the police is defective or collusive.
9. No doubt the deceased had a clear line of vision and could not have missed seeing the lorry which was parked ahead on the road.

But the very act of the driver of the lorry in parking the said vehicle on a busy road that too without putting on the indicators or giving any signal itself depicts that he did not exercise the degree of care which is expected of a prudent driver.
It is true that the accident occurred at 11.00 a.m. Meaning thereby there was sufficient light at that time.
But what also deserves notice is that the accident occurred on a road, the width of the said road is only 20 feet.
Further the said road connects to the Ballary road where the vehicles normally are permitted to go in slow speed because the said road is two way road.
In this view of the matter lesser degree of negligence has to be attributed on the part of the deceaed.

The driver of the lorry who had failed to adhere to the basic rules & regulations and acted in a gross negligent manner in parking the lorry on the said road without giving any indication had contributed a higher degree of negligence in the occurrence of the resultant accident.
Hence negligence is fixed on the rider / deceased and driver of lorry in the ratio of 10 : 90 respectively.
As such, this Tribunal answers issue No.2 Partly in the Affirmative.
10. ISSUE NO.1 :
The petitioners claim that petitioner No.1 is the wife, petitioner No.2 is the minor children and petitioner No.3 & 4 are the parents of the deceased.
To prove the same, petitioner No.1 filed affidavit in lieu of her chief- examination and deposed about the above relationship.
The Aadhar cards of petitioners are marked at Ex's.P.10 to 16 and contents of the police papers do fortify the said fact.
It is pertinent to note that this relationship of the petitioners with the deceased has not been disputed by the respondents.

Since the evidence led by the claimants is satisfactory and also taking into consideration the fact that there are no rival claimants, this Tribunal hold that the claimants are the legal representatives of the deceased.
Therefore, claimants are the legal heir and dependents of deceased.
Hence, this Tribunal answers issue No.1 In the Affirmative.
11. ISSUE NO.3:
In this case the petitioners have claimed the compensation of Rs.50,00,000/- on the death of deceased in the road traffic accident.
The petitioners contended that deceased was working as driver with Mr. Veeresh and earning Rs.30,000/- p.m.
In order to substantiate the above said fact the petitioners have examined one witness as PW.2.
He deposed that he was working as Teacher at Government School, Bellary District and deceased was working with him as a driver and Surekha vs Muthar Pasha

.M.F on 8 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/40758423/
4 as on the date of accident he was paying a sum of Rs.30,000/- p.m and Rs.200/- per day to the deceased.
During the course of cross-examination except denial suggestion nothing was elicited to prove that he has paid Rs.50,000/- to the deceased.
When this aspect being elicited during the course of cross examination of PW.2, only the basis of evidence and Ex.P.21, the income the deceased salary cannot be ascertained.
In the absence of any corroborative piece of evidence his salary cannot be ascertained.
Hence, viewed from that angle also Ex.P.21 was not valid in the eye of law.
The petitioners have not produced any documents to show the deceased was earning Rs.50,000/- p.m in the absence of which notional income is to be considered.

12. It is relevant to rely on a decision of Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka rendered on Division Bench in the case of Ananda v/s Arjun and another in MFA.No.101144/2020 (MV)
dated.05.07.2023.

entities.text: Ananda v/s Arjun and another in MFA.No.101144/2020 (MV)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Wherein the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka has laid down the following principles in para No.8(b) are as here under :
"(b) The accident is of the year 2017.
The Tribunal has assessed the income of the deceased at Rs.7,000/- per month as against the claim of Rs.2,50,000/- per annum.
To substantiate the said claim, the injured claimant has not placed any material on record, it is for the Courts and Tribunals to assess the income notionally.
The notional income fixed by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority for the accident of the year 2017 is Rs.10,250/-.

In the absence of any material produced by the claimant to prove his income, it is appropriate to assess the notional income of the injured claimant at Rs.10,250/-
per month, and the same is assessed as the monthly income of the injured claimant"
As such this court is taking the notional income as prescribed by the Karnataka Legal Service Authority, Bengaluru.
Therefore in view of the above decision, the accident was occurred in the year 2023.
Therefore, Rs.16,000/- p.m has to be taken into consideration as monthly income of the deceased.

13. So far as the age of the deceased is concerned, the petitioners have produced the Aadhar card to show the age of the deceased as per Ex.P10 wherein the date of birth of deceased is shown as 01.06.1986, which indicates that he was aged (37 years 6 months 29 days) 38 years on the date of accident.

Therefore the appropriate multiplier as per Sarla Verma's case for the said age group is '15'.
14.

As per the decision of Hon'ble Apex Court reported in 2017 ACJ 2700 (SC) (National Insurance Company Limited Vs Pranay Sethi and others), if the person died in the motor accident, the income with respect to the future prospect has to taken into consideration while awarding compensation.

entities.text: 2017 ACJ 2700 (SC) (National Insurance Company Limited Vs Pranay Sethi and others)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The Hon'ble Apex Court has provide the chart for age of the deceased and percentage for future prospects in between below the age of 40 years 40%, 40 years to 50 years 25% and 50 to 60 years 10%.
The deceased is not a permanent Employee and not a fixed salary person and he died at the age of 38 years.
Therefore, in this case, 40% income has to be taken into consideration for future prospects.

Further as stated above that, as on the date of accident, deceased aged about 38 years and Surekha vs Muthar Pasha .M.F on 8 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/40758423/
5 as such, 40% is added to the income of the deceased, then it comes to Rs.22,400/- p.m.
(Rs.16,000/- + 6,400/- i.e. 40%).
15.

entities.text: Surekha vs Muthar Pasha .M.F on 8 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The deceased died living behind 4 dependents.

As per principle laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in Sarala Verma Case, 1/4th of his income is required to be deducted towards his personal expenses which comes to Rs.16,800/- p.m. (Rs.22,400 - Rs.5,600 = Rs.16,800/-).
16. The income of the deceased is taken as Rs.16,800/- p.m. and the multiplier '15' is applied, then the loss of dependency comes to Rs.30,24,000/- (Rs.16,800/- X 12 X 15).
Considering the above facts, this Tribunal deems it just and reasonable to grant for compensation of Rs.30,24,000/- under the head of loss of dependency.

17. Further, as Law laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in National Insurance Company Limited Vs. Pranay Sethi and others, the compensation towards loss to estate, funeral expenses and consortium is to be awarded.

entities.text: National Insurance Company Limited Vs. Pranay Sethi and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The petitioners contended that they have spent substantial amount towards transportation of dead body, funeral and obsequies etc., but no documents are produced.

Hence this Tribunal award Rs.18,150/- towards loss to estate and Rs.18,150/- towards funeral expenses as enhanced at the rate of 10% on every 3 years and Rs.48,400/- towards consortium to the petitioner No.1.
By applying the observations made in the aforesaid case, as more than 6 years elapsed from the date of order amount of consortium, funeral expense and loss of estate to be enhanced.
18. In this case, the petitioner No.2 is the children and the petitioner No.3 & 4 are the parents of the deceased and

as per the decision reported in (2018) 12 SCC 130 in the case of Magma General Insurance Company Limited V/s Nanu Ram alias Chuhru Ram and others, the petitioner No.2 to 4 are entitled for filial consortium, as the filial consortium is the right of the parents and children to get compensation in the case of an accidental death of a children and father as the case may be.

entities.text: Magma General Insurance Company Limited V/s Nanu Ram alias Chuhru Ram and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: An accident leading to the death of a father cause great shock and agony to the children of the deceased and they lost their love and affection towards his/her father, as well as Petitioner no.3 & 4 towards deceased their son.
Therefore, petitioner No.2 to 4 are entitled for Rs.40,000/- each under the head of Filial consortium.

19. The calculation table stands as follows :
 Compensation heads Compensation  amount  1. Towards loss of dependency Rs.30,24,000/-
 2. Towards loss of Consortium to Rs. 48,400/-
 the petitioner No.1
3 . Towards loss to estate Rs. 18,150/-

4. Towards transportation of dead Rs. 18,150/-
 body funeral and obsequies  ceremony expenses  5. Towards loss of Filial consortium Rs. 1,20,000/-

6

Total Rs.32,28,700/-
 Less 10% towards contributory Rs. 3,22,870/-
 negligence on the part of the  deceased

Total compensation awarded Rs.29,05,830/-
20.
REGARDING INTEREST & LIABILITY:
Having regard to the nature of the claim and current bank rate of interest, this Tribunal is of the view that if interest at the rate of 6% p.a is awarded it would meet the ends of justice.
21. There is no dispute with regard to the issuance of insurance policy and its validity as on the date of accident.

Therefore, the respondent No.1 & 2 being the owner and insurer of the offending Lorry are jointly and severally liable to pay the aforesaid award amount to the petitioners together with interest @ 6% p.a. from the date of claim petition till realization of the entire amount.
However the respondent No.2 being the insurer is primarily liable to satisfy the award amount together with interest within two months from the date of this order.
Accordingly, I answer the issue No.3 Partly in the Affirmative.
22. ISSUE NO.4 :

In view of the discussion made supra, this Tribunal proceeds to pass the following :
ORDER
The petition filed under Section 166 of M.V. Act 1988, is hereby partly allowed with costs in the following terms :
The petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.29,05,830/- with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of claim petition till realization of the entire award amount.
The respondent No.2 is liable to pay and directed to deposit the compensation amount within a period of Two months from the date of award.

On deposit of the award amount together with interest, the claimants are entitled for the compensation amount by way of apportionment as follows :
 Petitioner No.1 - 25%
 Petitioner No.2 - 25%
 Petitioner No.3 - 25%
 Petitioner No.4 - 25%
Out of the share amount of Petitioner No.1, 3 & 4 a sum equal to 30% shall be deposited in their names in any Nationalized or Scheduled Bank of their choice for a period of 3 years and the remaining 70% shall be released to them through Surekha vs Muthar Pasha .M.F on 8 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/40758423/
7 E-payment on proper identification and verification.
However the said petitioners are at liberty to withdraw the periodical interest accrued on their deposit amount from time to time.

The share amount apportioned in the name of minor petitioner No.2 is ordered to be deposited in his name vide Fixed Deposit till he attains the age of majority, at any Nationalized/ Scheduled Bank as per the choice of the next friend/Natural guardian of the said minor petitioner.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw an award accordingly.
